data.source_title: Impact of Electronic Medical Record Training on Pediatric Residents’ Learning Outcomes: A Simulation-Based Study
data.locator: Abstract; Methods—Study design, Participants and Simulations; Results—Primary outcome; Table 1 and Figure 1
data.source_setting: Single-center prospective, parallel, non-blinded randomized controlled study at Riley Children’s Health, Indianapolis, using Cerner and simulated pediatric sepsis and respiratory-distress encounters.
data.source_period: August 2021–June 2022; follow-up simulations 3–6 months after baseline.
data.source_n: 32 first-year pediatric residents randomized 1:1 (16/group); 28 completed baseline and follow-up (14/group). All recruited residents participated in baseline simulations. Participants were from pediatrics, child neurology, neurodevelopmental, and child psychiatry; medicine-pediatrics residents excluded.
data.quantity: Change in EMR proficiency checklist score, sepsis scenario, baseline to follow-up; group means with 95% CI
data.source_evidence_basis: Randomized intervention received structured debriefing plus EMR-specific training; control received the same debriefing without EMR training. Authors report significantly greater improvement in the trained group for sepsis EMR checklist score. The secondary outcomes assessed simulated decision making/performance, not care delivered to actual patients.
data.limitations: Small single-site cohort; non-blinded; local Cerner-specific checklist; 4/32 randomized participants did not complete follow-up. Both groups had simulation/debriefing exposure; contrast estimates the additional EMR training intervention in this setting. Findings are learner assessment and simulated clinical performance only, not actual patient outcomes. Authors explicitly state actual-clinical-setting improvement remains to be demonstrated.
data.inferred_scenario_use: Supports a cautious hypothesis that structured EHR training may improve data-gathering proficiency in subsequent simulated cases. It does not validate EHRGym, establish transfer from agent task rewards to clinician competence, or show fewer errors/mortality/LOS in real patients. For local evaluation, predefine human learner outcomes and a later clinical-transfer study.
